[![Image 5](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/1/1e/Patricia_2015-10-23_1730Z.jpg/250px-Patricia_2015-10-23_1730Z.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Patricia_2015-10-23_1730Z.jpg)

[Hurricane Patricia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia "Hurricane Patricia") shortly after reaching its record peak intensity on October 23, 2015, while approaching Western Mexico

This is a **list of notable Pacific hurricanes**, subdivided by reason for notability. Notability means that it has met some criterion or achieved some statistic, or is part of a top ten for some superlative. It includes lists and rankings of [Pacific hurricanes](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_hurricane "Pacific hurricane") by different characteristics and impacts.

Characteristics include extremes of location, such as the northernmost or most equator-ward formation or position of a tropical cyclone. Other characteristics include its central pressure, windspeed, category on the [Saffir–Simpson scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffir%E2%80%93Simpson_scale "Saffir–Simpson scale"), [cyclogenesis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclogenesis "Tropical cyclogenesis") outside of a normal [hurricane season's](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pacific_hurricane "Pacific hurricane") timeframe, or storms that remain unnamed despite forming after tropical cyclone naming began in 1960. Another characteristic is how long a system lasted from formation to dissipation. These include the cost of damage, the number of casualties, as well as meteorological statistics such as rainfall point maximum, wind speed, and minimum pressure.

## Impact

### Retired names

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Retired names")]

Main article: [List of retired Pacific hurricane names](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_retired_Pacific_hurricane_names "List of retired Pacific hurricane names")

The following names have been retired in the East Pacific (in chronological order): [Hazel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_Storm_Hazel_(1965) "Tropical Storm Hazel (1965)"), [Adele](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Adele_(1970) "Hurricane Adele (1970)"), [Fico](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Fico "Hurricane Fico"), [Knut](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_Storm_Knut_(1987) "Tropical Storm Knut (1987)"), [Iva](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Iva_(1988) "Hurricane Iva (1988)"), [Fefa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Fefa "Hurricane Fefa"), [Ismael](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Ismael "Hurricane Ismael"), [Pauline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Pauline "Hurricane Pauline"), [Adolph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Adolph_(2001) "Hurricane Adolph (2001)"), Israel, [Kenna](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Kenna "Hurricane Kenna"), [Alma](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_Storm_Alma "Tropical Storm Alma"), [Manuel](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Manuel "Hurricane Manuel"), [Odile](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Odile "Hurricane Odile"), Isis, [Patricia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia "Hurricane Patricia"),[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-HRD-1)[Dora](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Dora_(2023) "Hurricane Dora (2023)"), [Otis](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Otis "Hurricane Otis"),[[2]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-WMO24-2) and [John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_John_(2024) "Hurricane John (2024)").[[3]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-WMO25-3)

In addition, the following names have been retired in the Central Pacific (in chronological order): [Iwa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Iwa "Hurricane Iwa"), [Iniki](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Iniki "Hurricane Iniki"), [Paka](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Typhoon_Paka "Typhoon Paka"), and [Ioke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Ioke "Hurricane Ioke").[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-HRD-1)

From the lists above, the names Hazel and Adele were retired for unclear reasons.[[4]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-HazelAdeleRetirement-4) Also, the names Adolph, Israel, and Isis were retired because of political considerations.[[1]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-HRD-1) In particular, the name Isis was pre-emptively removed in 2015 from the list of names for 2016 after being deemed inappropriate because of the [eponymous militant group](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Islamic_State "Islamic State").[[5]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-retired-5)

### Naming history

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Naming history")]

[![Image 9](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/b/b3/Oho_2015-10-06_2310Z.jpg/250px-Oho_2015-10-06_2310Z.jpg?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Oho_2015-10-06_2310Z.jpg)

[Hurricane Oho](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Oho "Hurricane Oho"), the eighth system to receive a central Pacific name in 2015

Naming of tropical cyclones in the eastern north Pacific began in the [1960 season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1960_Pacific_hurricane_season "1960 Pacific hurricane season"). That year, four lists of names were created. The plan was to proceed in a manner similar to that of the western Pacific; that is, the name of the first storm in one season would be the next unused one from the same list, and when the bottom of one list was reached the next list was started. This scheme was abandoned in 1965 and next year, the lists started being recycled on a four-year rotation, starting with the A name each year.[[47]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-ATWC-51) That same general scheme remains in use today, although the names and lists are different. On average, the eastern north Pacific sees about sixteen named storms per year.[[48]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-NCDC_2006_summary-52)

## Duration records

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records&action=edit&section=18 "Edit section: Duration records")]

[![Image 13](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/d/d2/Tina_1992-09-30_1801Z.png/250px-Tina_1992-09-30_1801Z.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=parser&utm_content=thumbnail)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/File:Tina_1992-09-30_1801Z.png)

[Hurricane Tina](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Tina_(1992) "Hurricane Tina (1992)"), the longest-lasting Pacific hurricane east of the International Date Line

This lists all Pacific hurricanes that existed as tropical cyclones while in the Pacific Ocean east of [the dateline](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/180th_meridian "180th meridian") for more than two weeks continuously. Hurricanes John and Dora spent some time in the west Pacific before dissipating. John spent eleven days west of the dateline; if that time was included John would have existed for a total of 30 days and 18 hours, while including Dora's time in the west Pacific would mean that it existed for 18 days.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-EPAC_HURDAT-53) One Atlantic hurricane, [Hurricane Joan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Joan%E2%80%93Miriam "Hurricane Joan–Miriam"), crossed into this basin and was renamed Miriam,[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-E15-69) giving it a total lifespan of 22 days,[[64]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-HURDAT-70) but not all of that was in the Pacific. 1993's Greg formed from the remnants of [Tropical Storm Bret (1993)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_Storm_Bret_(1993) "Tropical Storm Bret (1993)").[[63]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-E15-69) Its time as an Atlantic system is excluded.

All of these systems except Trudy, Olaf, Connie and Lala existed in both the east and central Pacific, and all except Olaf were hurricanes. Hurricane Trudy of 1990 is thus the longest lived eastern Pacific hurricane to stay in the eastern Pacific. Tropical Storm Olaf of 1997 is hence the longest-lived eastern Pacific tropical cyclone _not_ to reach hurricane intensity.[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-EPAC_HURDAT-53)

Prior to [Hurricane Lala](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Lala "Hurricane Lala")[_[citation needed](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wikipedia:Citation\_needed "Wikipedia:Citation needed")_], no known tropical cyclone forming in the central north Pacific lasted for longer than 14 days without crossing into [another basin](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tropical_cyclone_basins "Tropical cyclone basins").[[49]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-EPAC_HURDAT-53) The pre-2026 tropical cyclone that formed in the central Pacific and spent the most time there was [Hurricane Ana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Ana "Hurricane Ana"), at 12.75 days from formation to extratropical transition.[[65]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-AnaTCR-71)[[66]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-tc_records_CPHC-72)

The hurricane may or may not have made landfall in [San Diego County](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/San_Diego_County,_California "San Diego County, California"), due to uncertainty in the track reconstruction. ## Worldwide cyclone records set by Pacific storms

[[edit](https://en.wikipedia.org/w/index.php?title=List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records&action=edit&section=39 "Edit section: Worldwide cyclone records set by Pacific storms")]

*   **Highest official wind speed ever recorded in a tropical cyclone**: [Hurricane Patricia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia "Hurricane Patricia") with maximum sustained winds of 215 mph (345 km/h).[[162]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-D14-168)
*   **Fastest intensification (1-minute sustained surface winds)**: [Hurricane Patricia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Patricia "Hurricane Patricia") 55 [m/s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metre_per_second "Metre per second") (120 mph, 105 [kt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knot_(unit) "Knot (unit)"), 195 km/h), from 40 [m/s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metre_per_second "Metre per second") (85 mph, 75 [kt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knot_(unit) "Knot (unit)"), 140 km/h) to 95 [m/s](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Metre_per_second "Metre per second") (205 mph, 180 [kt](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Knot_(unit) "Knot (unit)"), 335 km/h) in under 24 h[[163]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-TCR1-169)
*   **Farthest-travelling tropical cyclone**: [Hurricane John](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_John_(1994) "Hurricane John (1994)") travelled for 13,180 km.[[164]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-noaafaq2-170)[[165]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-171)
*   **Highest [Accumulated cyclone energy (ACE)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Accumulated_cyclone_energy "Accumulated cyclone energy") index for a tropical cyclone**: [Hurricane Ioke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Ioke "Hurricane Ioke") achieved an ACE index of 85.[[166]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-172)
*   **Tropical cyclone at Category 4 or 5 intensity on the [Saffir–Simpson scale](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Saffir%E2%80%93Simpson_scale "Saffir–Simpson scale") for the longest**: [Hurricane Ioke](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hurricane_Ioke "Hurricane Ioke") was at that intensity for 198 consecutive hours.[[110]](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_Pacific_hurricane_records#cite_note-CPHC_2006-116)
